decisions.rationale: Exhaustive comparison found no same boundary: the anchor is the non-authority of stored resume/project convenience state, while PF-0110 only normalizes route identities and source-realization detail.
No comparator owns the MCP/provider boundary with its mirrored vocabulary and compatibility aliases; the listed refs are analogous owner-boundary controls for FileSafe and GitHub auth only.

The anchor governs headless browser/research evidence outputs and interrupted manifests; comparators address execution context, FileSafe observability/redaction, or visualizer metadata with different producers, lifecycles, and failures.

No comparator combines executable provenance, worktree path races, adapter creation, child environment inheritance, and secret handling under the same execution boundary; listed items cover proper subsets.
Preview/build sessions have their own command, result, artifact, cancellation, and stale-result boundary; comparator GUI and projection-state gaps are adjacent patterns, not that lifecycle.

The anchor concerns transactional Docker/GitHub build mutations and atomic source/auth snapshots; listed refs concern generic GUI mutation transitions, FileSafe host cleanup, or authority-domain separation.

No comparator defines the same debug-attachment identity, authorization lifetime, disappearance, backend negotiation, and cleanup race; daemon revocation and generic DAP reliability are plausible neighbors only.
The anchor is a cross-cutting atomic authorization-to-dispatch and cleanup-recovery protocol; each listed comparator covers only one revocation, child, daemon, host-effect, or cleanup seam.

No comparator governs retirement of the deprecated auth alias with owner, telemetry, deadline, version, and removal oracle; spelling, label compatibility, and a retired bridge are distinct migrations.

The Docker auth-result schema, consumers, redaction, and retention form a distinct payload lifecycle; comparator execution snapshots, GUI identities, and GitHub stable identity do not share its authority or outcome.

Docker execution, Hub management API, and Unraid XML authority are specifically separated; FileSafe and GitHub owner/domain boundaries are analogous but govern different authorities and failure semantics.
The mandatory repository-creation confirmation has repository race, permission, progress, and retry states; comparator approval and disclosure cards have different actions and lifecycle boundaries.

Build-to-Unraid is a compound publish transaction across build, template, Git commit, push, and reporting; the listed destructive, mutation, host, and cleanup controls are components or analogues, not equivalents.
The evidence overlay needs cross-document precedence, version compatibility, propagation, and conflict resolution; comparator ownership and adjacent-input rules do not govern that overlay contract.
The anchor spans child lineage on every lifecycle path plus tool, write, FileSafe, mode, provider/model/account, and crew ceilings; FileSafe child-clamp and freshness items are narrower members.

Delegated browser evidence has URL, cookie, form, console, iframe-origin, view-disclosure, and retention boundaries; preview sandbox, FileSafe redaction, debug capture, and approval races are separate surfaces.

The containerized-host child clamp and missing executable host-authority fixture are distinct from FileSafe child dispatch, freshness, and host-side-effect cleanup, despite dependency and vocabulary overlap.

The anchor is the contradiction between coordination registration/update warn-and-continue prose and fail-fast await code; audit/event-write failure handling is related but has different operations and outcomes.

SCM snapshots expose repo_root and worktree_path to GUI/receipts without a disclosure lifecycle; broader execution-context and identity-surface privacy gaps do not share this payload or consumer boundary.

Optional raw CLI evidence logs conflict with the unified run-history stream; FileSafe's singular seglog authority and event surfaces express the same architectural pattern for a different owner and event family.
Planning-child read-only authority under ask/plan mode is not the FileSafe pre-spawn child clamp; the latter is related dispatch authority but has different mode, user outcome, and failures.

The anchor is a specific retired-tier projection masquerading as active execution authority; requested/effective state, projection freshness, and action-gate contracts are adjacent safeguards, not that mapping.
The anchor governs retained/displayed raw provider, tool, and LLM payloads end to end; comparators govern execution context, GUI settlement, credential snapshots, debug capture, or attachments only.

A configured vision_provider being permitted to remain operationally dead is a wiring and requested/effective-disclosure gap; image-ingestion permission and general effective-state presentation remain distinct.
The anchor leaves required execution-field failures eligible for warn-and-continue; FileSafe guard initialization contracts fail closed for different state and authority boundaries.

Verification simultaneously mandates canonical seglog/redb persistence and a forbidden verification.log; FileSafe canonical-event and write-failure items are related patterns with different event authority.

Crew-board message confidentiality, retention, and cross-agent prompt-injection form a coordination-message boundary; attachment and compiled-prompt gates are downstream safeguards, not merge-equivalent.

The safe-hook envelope combines compatibility state, execution budget, permission checks, and fallback for platform hooks; comparator sandbox, daemon, child, and cleanup controls cover distinct participants.

Browser recording representation requires injection-warning and redaction provenance invariants; the listed preview, redaction, debug, image, and approval features touch separate surfaces or lifecycle stages.

The anchor classifies coordination mirrors and GUI concept sources as non-canonical lineage; artifact traversal, adjacent-input authority, and route normalization do not share that canonical-source decision.
All 212 comparators were reviewed; none governs graph-level node-ID uniqueness, dependency referential integrity, topology validation, and its failure oracle under the same runtime graph authority.

Plan-node change-budget path semantics and node/overlay policy-mode divergence are upstream plan authority; FileSafe write-scope precedence, empty allowlist, and request isolation are downstream related controls.

The anchor is the broad runtime-artifact producer, actor, provenance, consumer, and routing authority; envelope traversal and event/owner controls are members or adjacent authorities rather than equivalents.
The anchor is the cross-document runtime-artifact retention, privacy, deletion, and recovery lifecycle; comparator items each govern one specialized data class or consumer surface.

The anchor governs the HITL approval artifact and decision lifecycle broadly; FileSafe approval cards, recovery UI, override grants, and clipboard approval safety are specialized members with different states.

Immutable pre-dispatch permission snapshots bind a particular dispatch decision; revocation, daemon loss, pre-execution enforcement, and child freshness are related transitions but not that snapshot authority.

Logout/project-delete sensitive-residue cleanup has principal/project termination triggers; approval revocation, FileSafe never-delete edge cases, and cleanup/write-scope precedence have different triggers and outcomes.

The anchor is the umbrella separating ephemeral, scrubbed, exported, and credential-store evidence with masking and no-persist/no-echo rules; listed features are narrower redaction or prompt-storage controls.

The anchor coordinates selection-version fencing, mutation locks, revalidation, reconciliation, and explicit override; CAS, recovery episodes, GUI transitions, mutation receipts, and override grants are components.

Deferred Usage export, compact-header, Doctor, cost-column, and alert-history surfaces share one unclosed security/lifecycle bundle; diagnostic, identity-export, analytics, and metrics items differ in product authority.

Usage-widget layout persistence, concurrent edits, removed versions, account repair links, and narrow-screen behavior are distinct from the general side-panel responsive layout and FileSafe config lifecycle.

The anchor governs evidence-identity conflicts, missing route targets, schema skew, and exact-record versus view export authorization; traversal, projection trust, route normalization, and GUI export privacy are separate seams.
The anchor is a cross-surface Usage fixture matrix for accessibility, localization, route focus, offline targets, reduced motion, and high contrast; comparator GUI contracts cover narrower surfaces.

Cache hit-rate denominators, savings price authority, retention-policy freshness, revocation, and cross-account aggregation form a cache-specific reporting lifecycle; generic recovery analytics and FileSafe metrics are only neighbors.

Usage anomaly rationale and budget-source attribution have their own tenant, provider-input, provenance, and deletion boundary; identity GUI data and FileSafe recovery analytics differ in authority and outcome.

Optional OTLP/Helicone-style export from redacted seglog projections has an exporter trust and executable conformance boundary; FileSafe observability, redaction, event authority, and analytics are dependencies or analogues.

WebCapabilityAffordance defines injected browser modes, seven operations, permission state, native-browser primacy, and fallback status; transport safety, policy authority, and approval races do not duplicate that capability model.

The anchor excludes raw secrets, full provider config, and provider-private prompt files from the injected web affordance; attachment scrubbing and compiled-prompt enforcement govern different data paths.

The nine persona web policies bind initiation triggers, common tool limits, read-only/mutation denial, visibility, dispatch, and evidence routing; generic permission authority and persona GUI rules are adjacent.

Visible web ask/deny decision-card truth concerns mandatory disclosure, decision reasons, accessibility, focus, and localization; approval race lifecycle and other UI disclosure contracts remain plausible but distinct neighbors.
